newsitem.title: GERMANY: Broad EMU start not primary goal - Buba's Gaddum.
newsitem.headline: Broad EMU start not primary goal - Buba's Gaddum.

text.p: Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said on Saturday that starting Europe's currency union in 1999 with as many members as possible should not be a goal in itself.

"It cannot be an aim in itself to extend the circle of EMU membership as broadly as possible from the start without taking into account credible and lasting fulfilment of convergence criteria," Gaddum said in the text of a speech.
"If individual potential participants take a little more time to prepare for currency union in order to join it later -- but "fit' - they will be doing themselves the greatest favour," Gaddum said.
Gaddum was addressing a conference of businessmen and bankers in Athens. A copy of his speech was made available in Frankfurt in advance.
Gaddum also said all the criteria which EU states must fulfil to participate in the launch of the euro were important, especially budgetary criteria.

"The Bundesbank assumes that we are dealing with a treaty that 15 states have approved and 15 parliaments have ratified and which one therefore cannot undermine on certain points, which do not seem to fully suit at present," he said.
Gaddum said smaller EU countries could be worst affected by failure to stick to convergence criteria by larger EMU members.
